Tiny models.
Built on Bedrock.

A fresh evaluation protocol, a managed reference library and a visible AWS evidence trail. Part II tests what a compact model can do with better retrieval—and demonstrates the Bedrock suite along the way.

01 / The hard requirement

Small must mean something verifiable.

We keep the proposed ≤5 GB portable weight-artifact limit. It is a definition of the underlying model’s compactness, not a claim about memory consumed inside Bedrock. Quantization is now explicit: the candidate’s published FP8 artifact qualifies; the earlier BF16-only proposal is superseded.

Recommended candidate · catalog verified

Ministral 3 3B Instruct

4.67 GB
4,672,099,184 bytes · publisher model.safetensors

Mistral describes a 3.4B language model + 0.4B vision encoder, approximately 3.8B total. The instruct checkpoint is FP8 with some BF16 tensors. Text-only questions are proposed here.

mistral.ministral-3-3b-instruct
Bedrock runtime · on-demand · ACTIVE in us-west-2.

AWS model card · Pinned publisher files

Evidence boundary

What is—and isn’t—confirmed

  • Confirmed: regional catalog listing, active lifecycle, on-demand route, publisher artifact size and Apache-2.0 license.
  • Not confirmed: account invocation entitlement, quota headroom, a successful request, Bedrock’s serving precision or physical runtime memory.
  • The read-only entitlement check encountered a local credential-refresh permission error. No inference probe was made.
  • The publisher reports fitting FP8 in 8 GB VRAM; that is a publisher claim, not our measurement.

If “tiny” must mean an AWS service with measured memory below 5 GB, this requirement is not verified. Managed hosting does not disclose that footprint.

The repository offers both model.safetensors and consolidated.safetensors as alternative layouts. We count one usable weight artifact, not both duplicates. AWS does not expose a hash proving that its hosted weights are byte-identical to the publisher file.

Search scope: a successful us-west-2 runtime catalog read, AWS model cards including Mantle-only models, and publisher metadata. This is not a claim that no other eligible model exists anywhere. Marketplace endpoints and Custom Model Import are not counted as ready-to-use serverless catalog matches.

Roster decision for review: start with one qualified candidate across three retrieval arms, or hold until a second tiny model is verified. A one-model study can test retrieval improvements; it cannot establish “the best tiny model.”
02 / Bedrock is the core

Managed inference, retrieval and evaluation.

Proposed source region: us-west-2. A bounded runner calls Bedrock services, saves evidence to S3 and exports reviewed static results. No EC2 GPU, model-weight loading, persistent inference endpoint or self-managed search cluster is proposed.

Proposed service flow · not provisioned
  1. 1. Approve and freeze
    Model, protocol, budget, region and limits.
  2. 2. S3 → Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base
    Frozen Wikipedia corpus, managed parsing, embeddings, index and hybrid retrieval.
  3. 3. Retrieval → optional Bedrock Rerank
    One search, or merge four searches and rerank the evidence. No-RAG bypasses both.
  4. 4. Bedrock Ministral → S3
    Generate a short answer. Save prompt, response, evidence, timings, usage and errors.
  5. 5. Deterministic scorer + Bedrock Evaluations
    Exact benchmark accuracy plus a small retrieval/answer-quality audit. Gold stays out of generator requests.
  6. 6. Reviewed exports → GitHub → Netlify
    Publish results beside the unchanged Part I archive. Stop dispatch and clean up retained resources.
Cyan · Bedrock servicesLime · orchestration and controls
Bedrock inference

Converse API

Use the catalog-listed Ministral ID, short output caps and fixed request settings. Pin model ID, API route, date, region and prompt bytes. No provisioned throughput or always-on endpoint.

Bedrock knowledge bases

Managed KB + S3 source

Use managed ingestion, embeddings and hybrid search. Disable built-in reranking for the controlled searches; use explicit Bedrock Rerank on the merged pool for the advanced arm.

Managed KB uses managedSearchConfiguration, not the custom-vector-store configuration. Region availability and configuration must pass preflight.

Bedrock evaluations

RAG quality + judge reports

Upload saved retrieval/response records to supported evaluation jobs. The documented bring-your-own-response path accommodates our multi-query pipeline without assuming native end-to-end integration supports every component.

Supporting AWS work: S3 manifests and artifacts, scoped IAM, CloudWatch usage/error logs, CloudFormation where supported, and a cumulative spend ledger. A local runner is sufficient for the first bounded job; managed orchestration can follow if it adds value. Guardrails are a separate labeled demonstration, because turning them on changes measured behavior.

03 / Controlled retrieval

Same model. Same questions. Better evidence?

N0 / baseline

No retrieval

Question and answer choices go directly to Ministral. No KB access, rewriting or reranking.

H3 / single search

One hybrid retrieve

Search the question stem once. Set managed KB reranking to NONE. Pack the top three complete chunks within the context limit.

MQHR3 / advanced

Four searches + rerank

Ministral generates three distinct short rewrites. Search the original stem and rewrites separately, up to 20 candidates each. Deduplicate, combine ranks, call Cohere Rerank 3.5 through Bedrock, then pack the best three chunks.

Multi-retrieve path
REWRITEOriginal stem + 3 frozen variants
→
RETRIEVE ×4Bedrock KB · hybrid · rerank off
→
MERGEDeduplicate · rank fusion · ≤80
→
RERANKBedrock Cohere → best 3
→
ANSWERConverse → A / B / C / D

Use the same dated corpus, managed index and 1,536-token evidence budget. Bound document lengths under the selected reranker’s token limits. Log every query, retrieved chunk, deduplication decision and reranked index. Cache evidence for quality comparisons; measure uncached latency separately.

Managed KB retrieval is hybrid-only; this is no longer a vector-only comparison. The advanced arm changes query count and reranking together. A later matched-pool ablation is needed to attribute improvement specifically to the reranker. Agentic retrieval is deferred: fixed four-query retrieval is easier to bound and reproduce.

04 / A new experiment

Keep the questions. Change the protocol.

Part II stands on its own. We do not need to reproduce Part I or claim a year-over-year score improvement.

MMLU + HellaSwag

Freeze 114 MMLU test items (two per subject) and 100 HellaSwag validation items. Each prompt requests one A/B/C/D answer. A deterministic parser compares it to the gold label; invalid responses and failed attempts remain visible.

One candidate × 214 questions × three arms = 642 generated answers. Two candidates would mean 1,284 answers, only after qualifying the second. Rewrite and evaluation calls are extra.

This is generated-answer accuracy, not the old likelihood or HellaSwag length-normalized accuracy. Show separate result panels and no direct trend line against 2025.

What Bedrock Evaluations adds

Start with a fixed 30-item development QA audit, grounded in the frozen corpus, across the two RAG arms. Evaluate saved retrieved passages and short answers for relevance, correctness and faithfulness using a supported judge.

The audit is separate from multiple-choice accuracy: a single-letter answer cannot demonstrate citation or factual faithfulness. Add reference answers/evidence, disclose the judge and selected metrics, and cap judge tokens. Evaluate BYO responses so generation is not repeated unnecessarily.

A larger judge is evaluation infrastructure, not a tiny contestant. If all auxiliary models must also be tiny, revisit judge eligibility before launch.

First smoke test: five MMLU development items and five HellaSwag training items, disjoint from the test panel, across three arms: 30 answers for one model. Two MMLU questions per subject cannot support subject rankings. Small gains may remain inconclusive; report paired deltas and uncertainty without promising significance.

05 / Costs you can inspect

A small pilot should stay small.

Keep the $200 total ceiling, aim for $100 or less, and cap the initial approved pilot at $20. These prices were read from AWS’s public pricing page on October 26, 2026. Recheck before launch.

ComponentPublished rateIllustrative one-model panel
Ministral 3B · US standard on-demand$0.10 / million input tokens
$0.10 / million output tokens		642 answers × assumed 2,000 input + 16 output tokens ≈ $0.13
Managed KB storage$5 / GB raw data / monthAssume 1 GB for one month: $5.00
Managed KB retrieval$1 / 1,000 calls214 × (one + four searches): $1.07
Cohere Rerank 3.5$2 / 1,000 query units214 queries: about $0.43 if each fits one billable unit
Illustrative subtotalNot a complete campaign quoteAbout $6.63

Not included in that subtotal: rewrite generation, judge prompts and outputs, QA audit generation, retries, S3, logs, taxes or a larger/longer-lived corpus. Long documents can increase rerank billing units. Actual corpus bytes and rates must be frozen in the launch plan.

Managed parsing, managed embeddings and the default managed reranker are included at the documented defaults. Our explicit Cohere reranker is charged separately. Bedrock’s automatic algorithmic evaluation scores have no additional evaluation fee beyond inference; judge-based evaluations charge judge tokens, including their prompts.

Launch-time controls

  • Reserve worst-case call and retry liability before dispatch.
  • Cap concurrency, output tokens, query count, retries and judge metrics.
  • Stop scheduling at 80% of a stage budget until remaining liability is reconciled.
  • No new Marketplace subscriptions or imported-model hosting without a separate review.

After each stage

  • Reconcile usage and infrastructure charges against the cumulative ceiling.
  • Delete the KB when no longer needed; retained indexes and S3 data still cost money.
  • Publish actual cost separately from this illustration.
  • Billing alerts are a backup, not a real-time hard cap.
06 / Your review

Approve the direction before any run.

  1. Tiny definition: accept the 4.67 GB published FP8 artifact as evidence of a compact underlying model, while labeling Bedrock’s precision and memory unknown.
  2. Roster: approve a one-model retrieval study first, or hold until a second qualifying tiny model is established. No bigger substitute is assumed.
  3. Method: generated-answer MMLU/HellaSwag plus a separate Bedrock RAG-evaluation audit. No comparison claim against Part I.
  4. Services: Bedrock inference, Managed Knowledge Base and explicit Rerank, Bedrock Evaluations, S3/IAM/CloudWatch, existing Netlify publication.
  5. Execution gate: restore credentials, verify account/model/region support, finalize judge and costs, then approve a bounded smoke test. This page does not launch anything.

The existing runner remains disabled. The EC2 / likelihood-scoring design is archived as v0.1, not the current implementation target.
